strokeOrder: draw the bar from left to right
lift, begin above the bar and slant down to the right through it, then without lifting hook back to the left
lift, draw the curve at the foot: down on the left, then out to the right along the base
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03056 file records ざ as five stroke paths in this order and direction: さ's three strokes (the bar, the slanting stroke with its hook and the curve at the foot), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are four pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03056.svg, hiragana ざ (U+3056 HIRAGANA LETTER ZA), five stroke paths kvg:03056-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are さ's strokes, the same paths as in its file for さ, kanji/03055.svg; s4 and s5 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.

notes: Second sign of ございます.
